subject: Recap + next steps: request/response contracts & streaming behavior
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Palmer <alex@quantumhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-01T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + next steps: request/response contracts & streaming behavior

Alex — thanks again for making time earlier. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we can scope implementation and get you a pilot estimate:

1) Integration surface
- You want a single endpoint to support: conversational chat (stateful), batch completions for bulk summarization, and an embeddings/reranker pipeline for semantic search.
- Primary SDKs: web backend (node/python) and mobile usage via a thin proxy.

2) Auth & routing
- Plan: API key for dev/prod with RBAC on routes; optional mTLS for the mobile proxy.
- We'd route heavy embedding/rerank batches to the Dedicated pool. Latency-sensitive chat stays on Hosted with streaming enabled.

3) Request/response contracts (open questions)
- Chat vs completions: need to decide on a single canonical schema for messages + metadata (user_id, session_id, turn_id).
- Tokenization: you mentioned token counting on your side — we should agree on max_tokens semantics and how stop sequences are applied for both streaming and non-streaming paths.

4) Structured output / tool calling
- You want the model to emit a JSON command + confidence and let a local tool dispatcher execute actions (lookup patient id, fetch claim). We'll propose a constrained schema and example prompt set.

5) Embeddings & rerank
- Batch embedding size, dimensionality, and candidate rerank strategy (dot vs cosine) — you flagged compliance retention windows too.

Next steps (proposed):
- Ben to draft an initial request/response JSON schema + sample SDK call patterns (by Tue 2026-11-03).
- Alex to share a sanitized API contract and a sample prompt list (attachments ok).
- Laura to propose a 30-min tech sync the week of Nov 8 to align on streaming SLOs and pilot metrics.

Attachments: I’ve included an internal example prompt set to illustrate structured output expectations.

Thanks — happy to tighten any of these bullets.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Date: 2026-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: request/response contracts & streaming behavior

Rishi — thanks for the clear writeup. Quick answers / clarifications from our side: 

- We attached a sanitized API contract (quantumhealth-api-contract-v1.pdf) and a short prompt set (example-prompt-set.jsonl).
- For embeddings: we currently use 1536-dimension vectors and prefer cosine similarity; candidate pool sizes will be 100-500 per query initially.
- Tokenization: our client-side meter uses the same tokenization library as OpenAI tiktoken; we’ll share exact counts for our typical prompts.

Open Qs: 
1) If we enable streaming for chat, how should we handle stop sequences for tool-calling responses where the model must emit strict JSON? Will streaming split the JSON across packets and complicate parsing?
2) For max_tokens, we want to enforce a hard cap per call but allow server-side truncation policy — how would Redwood surface truncated outputs vs complete outputs in analytics?

Happy to join the Nov 8 sync.

— Alex
Alex Palmer
Director, Product — Quantum Health
alex@quantumhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-2104

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Palmer <alex@quantumhealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: request/response contracts & streaming behavior

Alex — jumping in with a proposed technical approach for the chat vs completions and streaming JSON concerns. TL;DR: doable with a small protocol change on the client side.

1) Schema suggestion (short)- request: {"kind": "chat|completion|embedding", "payload": {...}, "meta": {"user_id": "", "session_id": ""}}
- chat payload: messages array (role, text, token_count_hint)
- completion payload: prompt string + stop sequences array

2) Streaming + JSON/tool-calling- For structured JSON outputs we recommend a delimited streaming mode: server emits a finalization token (e.g., "<JSON_END>") and chunk-level offsets. Client reconstructs chunks and validates JSON on final token. This avoids partial-JSON parsing issues and keeps token-level streaming benefits.
- Alternative: use function-calling API (structured blocks returned at the end) with interim plain-text stream for progressive UX.

3) Tokenization and max_tokens- We will expose both estimated_token_cost and final_token_count in the response metadata. For hard caps, Redwood will include a flag response.truncated = true and response.truncation_reason = "max_tokens" so analytics can segment truncated vs complete.

4) Embeddings/rerank pipeline- Batch embeddings should be sent as newline-delimited JSON lines; we’ll accept arrays up to 2048 items per request on Dedicated with a recommended chunk size of 256 to keep tail latency predictable.

I’ll attach a short sample node/python SDK snippet in the follow-up. Ben

— Ben Carter
Principal Engineer, Developer Tools — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Alex Palmer <alex@quantumhealth.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps: request/response contracts & streaming behavior

Ben — that delimiting approach for JSON makes sense. A couple follow-ups so we can finalize the security/compliance side: 

- Can the finalization token be rotated/namespace-scoped per-customer so itʼs not predictable in transit? We’d like to ensure payload markers aren’t a vector for injection.
- For analytics: will we get per-token timestamps or just aggregate counts? We need per-token timing to map slow tails to specific prompts in our SLA reports.

Also, for embeddings throughput — you mentioned 2048 item arrays; what does that look like in terms of memory and GPU contention on Dedicated? We want to avoid cross-tenant noisy neighbor issues.

Thanks, attaching a redacted example of our prompt sets (see example-prompt-set.jsonl).

— Alex
